description: Halo blight is a bacterial disease of beans caused by Pseudomonas syringae pv. phaseolicola. It is seedborne and thrives under cool, humid conditions.
distribution: Worldwide, especially in temperate and subtropical regions of North America, South America, Europe, Africa, and Asia.

leaf: Lesions expand and coalesce into large necrotic areas
Irregular brown necrotic spots as disease progresses
Severe cases: extensive defoliation, reduced vigor
pod: Dark, sunken lesions with greasy appearance

damage: Significant yield and seed quality reduction
Can cause complete crop failure in high-incidence fields
Weakened plants more susceptible to secondary infections
Quarantine restrictions due to infected seed lots

biology.survival: Persists in crop debris and contaminated plant surfaces

chemical_control: Seed treatments to prevent early infection
genetic_control: Planting resistant varieties to reduce reliance on chemicals

notes: Integrated management combining cultural, chemical, and genetic strategies is most effective
Strict seed certification and quarantine measures are important to prevent spread
